title: Connection declarations
description: The shape of lib/Settings/connections.json. An app lists its outside connections here, and integriq turns each entry into one connection row. Contract: hydra openspec/changes/connection-registry/design.md, section D2. Integriq's runtime check is lib/Service/ConnectionDeclarationValidator.php, which mirrors this file rule for rule.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editors.

app.description: The app id from appinfo/info.xml. Integriq refuses a file whose app differs from the app it was read from.

key.description: Unique within the file and frozen once shipped. A row is keyed by app and key.

order.description: Sort order on the page. Default 100.

settingsUrl.description: Absolute path into the Nextcloud instance. Omit it when no settings section exists.

requiredConfig.description: App-config keys of the declaring app. All non-empty means the settings are saved.

adapter.description: The adapter seam behind this connection.

configKey.description: App-config key that selects the adapter: a class name, a provider name or a JSON settings blob.

jsonPath.description: Dot path into the value when configKey holds a JSON object, such as chat.provider. A missing path reads as empty.

simulatedValues.description: The values that mean a mock adapter answers. Compared case-insensitively after trimming. Default: one empty string.

available.description: false means declared and not usable yet. Default true.

unavailableMessage.description: Why the connection is not usable.

unconfiguredMessage.description: Shown while nothing is known about the connection yet. Default: Not checked yet.

sourceTemplate.description: Slug of an integriq source template, offered first when an admin links a source.

reportedOnly.description: true means only the app can tell what answers. Integriq then skips the adapter and settings rules. Default false.
